items.title: 69537_Jimmy Jones oral history interview
items.q: Nat's got a lot of real estate and stuff... Fine musicians.

ctx.x: You know? They just didn't like that road. And they all went back -- they all went back home. They're doing well. Nat's got a lot of real estate and stuff, you know. He doesn't have to break his neck anymore. And they just play for fun, you know. Fine musicians. Just like the same situation I was speaking of -- the socio-economic thing

of Chicago. You know, the situation just sends you somewhere else, no matter what you started out to do. For survival you just have to adjust, you know. You have to keep your head above water, you know. And there's another thing, where drifting towards an Ellington type sound, because all of us admired the Ellington band. At that time, you know. We loved that band, you know? All the musicians loved it. And I think I was on my way, maybe simply because -- maybe that was one of the reasons I was with Tony [Fambro,]…
